newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy gets state OK to buy NYSEG stake.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy gets state OK to buy NYSEG stake.

text.p: The New York Public Service Commission said Wednesday it would permit independent power producer CalEnergy Co. Inc. to proceed with a hostile tender offer for 9.9 percent of New York State Electric & Gas Corp.
In a late afternoon statement, the state regulator said it had determined the tender offer "poses no threat to ratepayers and does benefit the holders of the stock in question."
NYSEG had asked the commission to prohibit the $24.50 per share tender offer from proceeding.

However, NYSEG spokeswoman Katherine Karlson said in a statement issued late Wednesday that the company has been validated by the ruling, because the commission has not prejudged whether a takeover of NYSEG would be endorsed.

"CalEnergy must now abide by a formal process which will give careful and deliberate consideration to CalEnergy's fitness and qualifications to be entrusted with the management of a complex electric and natural gas distribution system in New York," Karlson said.
CalEnergy has launched the $159 million tender offer as the first step of a plan to buy the whole utility in a transaction valued at $1.9 billion.

In seeking to block the tender offer, which expires on Thursday, NYSEG had cited a portion of the state's Public Service Law, which it contended requires companies to receive commission approval before acquiring securities of a gas or electric company.
CalEnergy had argued that it was entitled to buy less than 10 percent of NYSEG without prior commission approval.
The order officially was issued by commission Chairman John O'Mara and will be presented to the full commission for approval on Aug. 20.
Although the order approved the purchase of 9.9 percent of NYSEG shares, it also noted that the approval is separate from a decision on any future proposal regarding a NYSEG takeover.

"Any future commission analysis of additional purchases will address, among other things, the far more complex issue of whether the public interest will be served by CalEnergy's management of NYSEG," the commission said.
It also ordered CalEnergy to file for approval of any additional share purchases by no later than Aug. 29.

CalEnergy Chief Executive Officer David Sokol said the company will not extend the tender offer past Thursday's deadline and will walk away from the transaction if it does not receive shareholder support.
"If shareholders voice their opinion that we are not the right acquirer, then we respect that and move on," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I think our hope is that NYSEG will stop trying to put roadblocks in front of the shareholders so that they can accept our tender offer, or not, tomorrow," he said.
He also reiterated that CalEnergy would prefer a friendly transaction with NYSEG as opposed to the hostile approach.
NYSEG last month rejected the CalEnergy offer and last week told shareholders it would soon review its dividend policy and stock buyback plans.
NYSEG did not have any immediate comment on the commission's decision.
NYSEG's stock fell 50 cents to close at $25.25, while CalEnergy slid $1.31 to $35.44 on the New York Stock Exchange.
